text: Foundry Local's catalog is intentionally curated: chat models such as GPT OSS, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral and Phi, plus Whisper for audio transcription. Microsoft says it does not support every model because it targets shipping production apps, not general model experimentation. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-12)

Foundry Local is an embeddable SDK plus native runtime (C#, JavaScript, Rust, Python) that runs inference in-process and adds about 20 MB to an app package; the web server and CLI are optional development tools, not the core product. (high confidence)

Foundry Local uses ONNX Runtime and ONNX models from the Foundry Catalog, selected per device. Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp use GGUF. Developers lose GGUF-level quantization and backend choice such as Vulkan versus ROCm. (medium confidence)

A third-party reviewer reported Foundry Local 20-30% faster than Ollama on the same models on their own laptop. This is a single anecdote, not a benchmark. Microsoft's ONNX-versus-llama.cpp speed claims compare ONNX-optimized models, not matched GGUF quantizations. PromptQuorum's review quotes no benchmark numbers. (low confidence)
Foundry Local reached general availability on 2026-04-09, announced on the Microsoft Foundry devblog. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-09)

Foundry Local detects GPU, NPU and CPU and picks an execution provider automatically, falling back to CPU. On Windows it uses WinML; on macOS it uses the Apple Silicon GPU via Metal. (high confidence)

Foundry Local exposes OpenAI request/response formats, including the Responses API, via an optional OpenAI-compatible local web server. Existing OpenAI-SDK code can point at the endpoint with minimal changes. (high confidence)

Supported platforms are Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux. An Azure subscription is not required. Prompts and outputs stay on-device; the network is used only for model/execution-provider downloads and optional diagnostics. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-04)

Microsoft says Foundry Local is optimized for single-user, hardware-constrained devices and is not a server inference stack: it lacks concurrent request queuing and continuous batching, and Microsoft points multi-user serving to vLLM or Triton. (high confidence)

Foundry Local v2.1.0 added bring-your-own-model: it registers ONNX Runtime GenAI models in the local catalog without copying the files, from C++, C#, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript and Rust. Registered models use the same discovery, load and session APIs as catalog models. The release notes name no GGUF support. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Licensing is split: the Foundry Local SDK is MIT, the CLI is under Microsoft proprietary terms, and each catalog model carries its own license. Ollama is fully MIT. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-12)
